answer: Give governance weight to locked capital with a linear rule, not a fixed vote bonus per account. Every voting unit must reference a distinct unspent deposit, frozen until the ballot closes; the tally rejects reused deposits. If onyx splits its deposit between thread and vine accounts, their combined weight stays unchanged. More names buy no extra votes, and borrowing capital costs interest during the lock. This blocks identity multiplication, not wealth concentration: a rich attacker can still buy control, so avoid claiming it proves one person per vote.
